## A paired benchmark of biomedical agents in Galaxy and custom code

We assembled an archive of 4,240 agent runs on three benchmarks: BixBench-Verified-50, CompBioBench and workflows from the Intergalactic Workflow Commission (IWC) (Fig. 1).
Four Codex model configurations – GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna, and DeepSeek V4 Pro – attempted every task three times in each environment, yielding 3,840 assigned runs.
In the custom-code environment, agents installed software and wrote their own custom analysis code.
In the Galaxy environment, agents used only the Galaxy workbench to accomplish the task.
This includes the option to run the agent's own code as a Galaxy user-defined tool (UDT).
All 160 tasks were analyzed individually for each of the three replicates.

Each benchmark keeps its own endpoint.
BixBench uses an established ground truth set by the original creators and made publicly available.
Grades are those shown on the project's results site, which corrected the scoring of two items (bix-53-q2 and bix-43-q2) after the original evaluation.
CompBioBench uses an agreement with a reconstructed answer key, in which 54 references were inferred from recorded scores and 46 from predicted answers.
This is because the authors of the benchmark evaluated the answer but obscured the ground truth.
IWC uses continuous agreement, a scale from 0 to 1, with curated workflow outputs.
The correct answer is that the entire workflow executes as expected.
IWC workflows are designed to be Galaxy-specific, allowing a refined evaluation of the agents in the Galaxy workbench.
For all benchmarks, we recorded model input tokens, including cached context the model rereads, code written by the agent, and every call agents made to Galaxy.

The two environments dedicated to running the tasks differ in design.
Galaxy prompts specify an execution policy, including history use, permitted tools, UDT rules, and interface timeouts, whereas custom code has no detailed restrictions on how it can be executed.
Therefore, Galaxy prompts were longer than custom-code prompts on BixBench (707 versus 366 median words) and CompBioBench (938 versus 227) but not on IWC (333 versus 344).
Time budgets, runtime environments, and campaign histories also differ (Methods).
Our comparisons are driven by the environment, deployment, benchmark task, agent model, execution trajectory, answer, and replicates, rather than by an isolated effect of the Galaxy workbench's answer.

## Agents perform similarly in Galaxy and custom code

We first asked whether working in Galaxy changes how often agents reach the correct answer.
Overall performance was similar in the two envrionments (Fig. 2).
On BixBench, acceptance was 87.2% with custom code and 87.7% with Galaxy, a difference of +0.5 (-3.9 to 4.8) percentage points (estimate and 95% cluster-bootstrap interval; Fig. 2b).
On CompBioBench, agreement with the reconstructed key was 86.7% and 87.0%, a difference of +0.3 (-1.8 to 2.5) points (Fig. 2b).
Both differences stayed within about one point of zero when we removed 15 BixBench tasks with audited benchmark-side problems or 66 CompBioBench taks-configuration cells containing wrong answers or target scores (Extended Data Fig. 2b).
On IWC, output agreement over all ten tasks was 0.95 with custom code and 0.98 with Galaxy (+0.036 (0.006 to 0.074); Fig. 2b), and three tasks containing a zero-scored run accounted for most of this difference (Extended Data Fig. 2b).

<!-- Draft image image1.emf from the Word draft is not included. Figures are generated from code in figures/; see figures/README.md. -->

**Fig. 1 \| Study design: the same model configurations perform each task in the custom-code condition and in the Galaxy condition.** **a**, Custom-code condition, the reference condition.
The agent uses an unrestricted shell that can install and run any software.
Its execution trace records commands, scripts, command output and final files, but no individual analysis jobs.
b, Galaxy condition.
The same model configuration, run by the Codex agent harness, reaches the Galaxy server (usegalaxy.org) through the Galaxy interface, a Model Context Protocol server.
The interface offers tool search, tool parameter descriptions, analysis-history inspection, job submission and monitoring, and user-defined tools.
The execution trace and analysis history record tool identities and versions, requested and resolved parameters, datasets, job states and error messages.
The condition label records assignment; it does not certify that every operation ran inside Galaxy.
c, Run populations.
Each cell gives the number of runs (tasks × 3 replicate runs) per model configuration and execution condition.
BixBench-Verified-50 and CompBioBench are platform-neutral benchmarks; IWC is a workflow-derived benchmark.
Endpoints differ: accuracy for BixBench-Verified-50, reported benchmark scores for CompBioBench and output agreement for IWC.
The benchmarks are therefore analysed separately and never pooled (Supplementary Table 1).
DeepSeek V4 Pro (Claude Code, superseded) is reported separately.
GPT-6 Astra is unpaired and excluded from condition differences.
Archive totals: 4,240 runs, 4,228 execution traces, 23,080 Galaxy analysis jobs and 69,812 Galaxy interface calls (Extended Data Fig. 1a).

**Fig. 2 \| Performance is similar in the two execution conditions, and most scored-incorrect runs were not caused by Galaxy. a–c**, Condition difference (Galaxy − custom code) for each benchmark, with 95% confidence intervals.
Each estimate is printed beside its interval; positive values mean the Galaxy condition scored higher.
Model configurations occupy the same rows in every panel, followed by the four Codex model configurations pooled.
The line under each title gives the pooled condition-level summary for each execution condition.
a, BixBench-Verified-50: condition difference in accuracy, in percentage points (run population per condition: 50 tasks × 3 replicate runs per model configuration; Supplementary Table 2).
b, CompBioBench: condition difference in the mean reported benchmark score (answers credited, of 100) over three replicate runs per condition.
Open points have no interval, because the archive keeps only reported benchmark scores, some labelled predicted.
GPT-6 Astra (custom-code condition only, not paired) scored 93 (Supplementary Tables 5 and 6).
c, IWC: condition difference in mean output agreement over the ten tasks scored in both conditions (Supplementary Table 7).
d, IWC output agreement of every run on all ten tasks.
Ticks mark the mean of 12 replicate runs, and the axis is broken between 0.45 and 0.80.
Numbered notes give the cause of every run below 0.5, established from its execution trace.
e, Primary and secondary cause of every scored-incorrect BixBench-Verified-50 run of the four Codex model configurations (77 custom-code condition, 74 Galaxy condition), adjudicated from execution traces (Supplementary Table 14; Supplementary Note 6).

**Figure 3 \| Galaxy preserves final-answer accuracy on BixBench-Verified-50.** **a**, Overall accuracy across 600 runs per execution condition.
Galaxy achieved 87.7% accuracy (526/600), compared with 87.2% (523/600) for custom code, a difference of 0.5 percentage points.
**b**, Accuracy by model and execution condition across three independent replicates per question.
**c**, Number of incorrect runs for each question with at least one failure, partitioned by execution condition.
Each question comprised 12 runs per condition, for a total of 24 runs.
Five questions accounted for 97 of the 151 incorrect runs (64.2%).
**d**, Representative tasks with the largest condition-specific differences.
For bix-30-q3, Galaxy returned the accepted result in 12 of 12 runs compared with 4 of 12 custom-code runs; failed custom-code runs introduced analytical steps not specified by the task.
For bix-45-q1, custom code returned the accepted result in 8 of 12 runs, whereas Galaxy did so in 0 of 12 runs; the discrepancy resulted from a PhyKIT version mismatch between the Galaxy tool and the version associated with the accepted answer.

<!-- Draft image image6.png from the Word draft is not included. Figures are generated from code in figures/; see figures/README.md. -->

**Figure 4 \| Galaxy preserves CompBioBench accuracy with greater model interaction. a**, Overall accuracy across 2,400 runs.
Galaxy returned 1,044/1,200 correct answers (87.0%) versus 1,040/1,200 (86.7%) for custom code.
**b**, Accuracy by model and execution condition across three replicates of 100 tasks.
**c**, Total model tokens by model and condition; Galaxy used 14.15 billion tokens versus 5.19 billion for custom code overall (2.7-fold increase).
**d**, Representative condition-specific analytical trajectories for variant-status-q1 and reverse-search-gwas-q2, with contaminated-rna-q3 illustrating that trajectory-dependent accuracy differences were not uniformly directional.
